nodes.label: Capability Catalogue (risk classification as data)
nodes.rationale: Every capability is declared once with a risk level drawn from PRD 11.1. The catalogue is data rather than code so the risk classification is directly testable against the PRD - yet it lives in code, not a database row, because a capability addable by editing a row would be a capability addable without review.

nodes.label: Grant Scopes (ONCE, SESSION, TASK, APPLICATION, FOLDER, ALWAYS)
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS is accepted only for LOW risk. Folder grants match by canonical path prefix so a grant covers children and nothing else. Every evaluation, grant, revocation and expiry writes an audit event and publishes PermissionDecided - there is no silent path.
nodes.norm_label: grant scopes (once, session, task, application, folder, always)

nodes.label: ToolSpec (tool contract)
nodes.rationale: A tool is the only way the agent affects anything. The pydantic ToolSpec carries tool ID, version, description, input/output schemas, risk category, required capabilities, resource locks, timeout, retry policy, state-change flag, verification method, redaction rules, supported applications, failure codes and reversibility metadata.

nodes.label: Prohibited Tool Denylist (identity and pattern)
nodes.rationale: Registration rejects every prohibited tool name from PRD 13.3 by exact identity, and also names matching shell, powershell, cmd, terminal, wsl, exec, eval, subprocess, arbitrary, registry_write and similar, so a future contributor cannot introduce run_shell_v2. These are belt and braces; the real guarantee is that no such implementation exists.

nodes.label: tests/security/test_no_shell.py (AST scan of src/)
nodes.rationale: Scans the whole src/ tree for subprocess, os.system, os.popen, eval(, exec(, shell=True, ShellExecute and CreateProcess and fails the build if any appears. Phase 1 will need os.startfile, which will be introduced through a single reviewed allow-listed call site recorded in an ADR, not by weakening the test.

nodes.label: tests/security/test_layering.py
nodes.rationale: Asserts that only the presentation layer imports Qt and that no module imports a higher layer.

nodes.label: ToolInvoker (six-step pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Allow-list, schema validation, permission, resource locks, approval, execute - in that order. Schema validation precedes permission so the approval dialog shows validated concrete parameters rather than raw model output; locks are acquired before approval so a user is not asked to approve something that will then queue behind another task.

nodes.label: ApprovalPort
nodes.rationale: An interface, not the GUI: the core asks and the shell answers, so headless and test contexts substitute a policy object.

nodes.label: DenyingApprovalPort (silence is never consent)
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 default: if nothing is wired to ask the user, the answer is no. Consequently no capability requiring approval can run until the Phase 1 Qt dialog lands.

nodes.label: ToolResult (typed outcomes)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes succeeded, failed, denied, blocked, timed_out and cancelled, each with a failure code from the tool's declared set. There is no boolean 'worked'.

nodes.label: Success Requires Verification
nodes.rationale: Verification belongs to the tool, not the caller (PRD FR-048, AT-018). A tool that cannot verify its own effect reports unverified, and the task layer treats that as not-succeeded.

nodes.label: Ten-State Task Machine (jarvis.tasks.states)
nodes.rationale: Explicit transition table; every transition is validated and an illegal transition raises rather than silently correcting. Terminal states SUCCEEDED, FAILED and CANCELLED have no outgoing edges so recovery can never silently re-run finished work.

nodes.label: Task Store (jarvis.tasks.store)
nodes.rationale: SQLite-backed; transitions are written inside a transaction together with their audit event so the log and the state cannot disagree.

nodes.label: Resource Locks (jarvis.tasks.locks)
nodes.rationale: Named, exclusive, persisted, owner-attributed. Namespace: foreground_desktop, browser_profile, microphone_capture, speaker_output, clipboard, application, folder_scope, network_connector. Acquisition is all-or-nothing over a sorted set; a held lock records the runtime instance ID so startup reclaims locks whose owner instance is gone.

nodes.label: Task Scheduler (jarvis.tasks.scheduler)
nodes.rationale: One background thread selects QUEUED tasks by priority then age, attempts lock acquisition and dispatches to a bounded runner pool. Tasks whose locks are unavailable stay QUEUED with a visible waiting_on reason, which makes PRD AT-009 an observable property rather than an emergent accident.

nodes.label: Crash Recovery
nodes.rationale: On startup RUNNING and WAITING tasks from a previous instance become PAUSED with recovered=true and blocked_reason=interrupted_by_restart. They are never auto-resumed because resuming blindly could repeat a consequential external action. Stale locks are released and every recovery decision is audited.

nodes.label: LLM Boundary (jarvis.llm)
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 implements only the health check, but the boundary is defined now so later phases have somewhere to land. Structured output only: the planner will emit tool calls against JSON schemas generated from ToolSpec.input_schema, and free-form text can never reach the invoker.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Ollama Endpoint
nodes.rationale: The health checker rejects a configured base URL whose host is not a loopback address and audits the refusal, because a remote 'local' endpoint would silently ship every prompt off the machine. The endpoint is unauthenticated by design and any local process can reach it; Jarvis cannot fix that, only avoid trusting it (ADR-0007).

nodes.label: Offline Mode Enforced at the Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: In offline network mode the health check does not open a socket; it returns skipped(reason=offline_mode). PRD AT-001 is therefore a property of the adapter, not of caller discipline.
nodes.norm_label: offline mode enforced at the adapter boundary

nodes.label: Separate Model Roles (planner, vision, embeddings, STT, TTS)
nodes.rationale: Each role names a profile in configuration; nothing hard-codes a model name. The resource scheduler that prevents two heavy models loading at once is stubbed as configuration today (model_runtime.load_strategy: sequential).
nodes.norm_label: separate model roles (planner, vision, embeddings, stt, tts)

nodes.label: JarvisCore (composition root)
nodes.rationale: Owns startup and shutdown ordering and imports no GUI code. Startup: vault paths, config, SQLite plus migrations, EventBus and AuditLog, PermissionEngine/ToolRegistry/ToolInvoker, TaskStore/LockManager/TaskScheduler, crash recovery, tool registration, workers, AppStarted. Shutdown is the reverse and idempotent.

nodes.label: Emergency Stop
nodes.rationale: Cancels running tasks, releases every lock, halts workers and publishes EmergencyStopCompleted with a list of exactly what was stopped - but leaves the process running.

nodes.label: Single-Instance Guard
nodes.rationale: A Windows named mutex Local\ProjectJarvis.SingleInstance, per-session by design so it constrains one interactive session as the PRD requires. A lock-file fallback exists for non-Windows development hosts so the test suite stays portable.

nodes.label: Jarvis Shell (jarvis.ui tray and main window)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately thin: it renders state and collects user decisions. Tray icons are drawn programmatically with QPainter rather than shipped as assets, which sidesteps the asset-licensing constraint until an original icon set exists. Colour is never the only signal - each state also sets a tooltip and an accessible name.
nodes.norm_label: jarvis shell (jarvis.ui tray and main window)

nodes.label: Honest Degraded UI (disabled, not hidden, not fake)
nodes.rationale: Menu items whose feature does not exist are present but disabled with a tooltip naming the phase. Not hidden, so the shape of the product is visible; not fake, so nothing reports success it did not achieve. When a provider is unavailable the capability reports the limitation and the offered fallback and the tray shows a degraded state.
nodes.norm_label: honest degraded ui (disabled, not hidden, not fake)

nodes.label: Untrusted Content Enters as Delimited Observations
nodes.rationale: Web pages, documents and UI text attach to the task wrapped in delimiters and are never concatenated into the instruction region of a prompt. An observation can inform a plan; it can never authorise a capability. Specified but unexercised in Phase 0 - the delimiter strategy needs adversarial testing when the first content source lands in Phase 2.
nodes.norm_label: untrusted content enters as delimited observations

nodes.label: Planner Cannot Skip the Invoker
nodes.rationale: Tools are not callable objects handed to the model. The model emits a name and a parameter object, and only the invoker can resolve a name to an implementation.

nodes.label: Extension Points Table
nodes.rationale: Named protocols for each future capability: Tool, ApprovalPort, TtsProvider, SttProvider, WakeDetector, ChatProvider, AppAdapter, UiBackend, TaskRunner, SkillManifest and SecretStore. Adapters are in-process today; whether they become isolated plugins is open (ADR-0010).

nodes.label: Bounded Timeouts and Declared Retry Policy
nodes.rationale: Every external interaction declares a timeout - there is no unbounded wait. RetryPolicy is part of ToolSpec rather than ad-hoc at call sites, and the invoker rejects a result carrying an undeclared failure code so a tool cannot invent a vague error.
nodes.norm_label: bounded timeouts and declared retry policy

nodes.label: Five-Suite Test Architecture
nodes.rationale: unit, security, integration, ui (offscreen Qt) and acceptance (one test per Phase 0 exit criterion). Every test gets an isolated vault via JARVIS_DATA_DIR so none touches the real %LOCALAPPDATA%; none requires Ollama, a microphone, a GPU or the network. The security suite is load-bearing: it fails the build rather than warning.

nodes.label: Architectural Change Control
nodes.rationale: Changing a capability's risk classification requires an ADR; adding a denylist exemption requires an ADR and a named reviewer; new PySide6 imports outside jarvis.ui and any process-creation or dynamic-evaluation primitive fail tests/security. Section 12 must be accurate before a phase is declared complete.

nodes.label: In-Process Isolation Is Not a Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: In Phases 0-3 a defect in the automation worker can reach the vault. Process separation is knowingly deferred (ADR-0004) and recorded as a known gap so it is not discovered late.
nodes.norm_label: in-process isolation is not a security boundary

nodes.label: SQLite Is the Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Everything else - embedding indexes, file indexes, caches - is derived, rebuildable and must contain no unique information. Large or binary artefacts live on disk referenced by path and never become BLOBs. Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC text so the database stays inspectable with any tool and sorts correctly.
nodes.norm_label: sqlite is the single source of truth

nodes.label: UUID4 Hex Identifiers (jarvis.common.new_id)
nodes.rationale: 32-character opaque identifiers carrying no meaning, generated in one place.

nodes.label: Vault Storage Layout
nodes.rationale: config/, data/, logs/, attachments/, browser/, models/, exports/, backups/, temp/ and runtime/ under %LOCALAPPDATA%\ProjectJarvis. The whole vault relocates via --data-dir or JARVIS_DATA_DIR, and VaultPaths is the only code resolving any of these paths.

nodes.label: Two Audit Sinks, One Record of Truth
nodes.rationale: audit.jsonl is tamper-evident and the audit_event table is a search index over it. If the index is lost it can be rebuilt from the file; if the file is lost history is gone - which is why the file is written first and a SQLite failure degrades search rather than losing the entry.
nodes.norm_label: two audit sinks, one record of truth

nodes.label: runtime_instance table
nodes.rationale: One row per application launch. This is what makes crash detection possible: an instance with stopped_at IS NULL that is not the current one died.

nodes.label: audit_event table
nodes.rationale: Field set is PRD 11.5 exactly. parameters_json and pre_state_json are already redacted on the way in, and evidence_ref is a path, never inline content, so nothing downstream has to remember to redact.

nodes.label: permission_grant table
nodes.rationale: Absence of a row is never permission - no grant means ask or deny by policy. Invariants are enforced by PermissionEngine.grant rather than convention: prohibited risk can never be granted, high risk may only be allowed with scope once, always-allow is low risk only. Rows are never deleted; revocation sets revoked_at so the permission history stays auditable.

nodes.label: task table
nodes.rationale: The durable state machine, carrying parent_task_id for task trees, the declared lock set, attempts and max_retries, a user-visible waiting_on reason, a recovered marker and the instance_id of the launch that last ran it.

nodes.label: task_transition table
nodes.rationale: Written in the same transaction as the state change itself, so the log and the state cannot disagree.

nodes.label: task_checkpoint table
nodes.rationale: Durable resume points; UNIQUE (task_id, sequence) keeps them ordered and idempotent.

nodes.label: task_evidence table
nodes.rationale: A task is not succeeded because something was clicked; it is succeeded because this table says why. Artefacts are referenced by path into attachments/ and content is never inlined.

nodes.label: resource_lock table
nodes.rationale: The primary key IS the mutual exclusion - one row per lock name or no row - so there is no separate locking protocol to get wrong. instance_id is what makes stale locks identifiable. Unknown lock names are rejected at acquisition.

nodes.label: tool_invocation table
nodes.rationale: outcome and verification are separate columns on purpose: a tool that ran but could not confirm its effect is succeeded + unverified, which does not satisfy a task's success criteria.

nodes.label: Soft References So Audit Survives Its Subject
nodes.rationale: Only task-to-task, transition, checkpoint and evidence are enforced cascading foreign keys. The rest are soft references, because an audit record must survive deletion of the task it describes - otherwise deleting a task would erase the evidence of what it did.
nodes.norm_label: soft references so audit survives its subject

nodes.label: Frozen Pydantic Models per Persisted Entity
nodes.rationale: The database is the persistence format; the pydantic models are the contract. The capability catalogue and tool registry are deliberately code, not data, because a capability addable by editing a row would be addable without review.
nodes.norm_label: frozen pydantic models per persisted entity

nodes.label: Forward-Only Transactional Migrations
nodes.rationale: Released migrations are never edited; a correction is a new migration. Statements execute one at a time inside a single transaction because executescript would implicitly commit and defeat the all-or-nothing guarantee. A database newer than the running build is a hard startup failure, because best-effort reading could write records the newer schema depends on being shaped differently.

nodes.label: Retention and Deletion Rules
nodes.rationale: Cascade is the default for derived data; audit records survive their subject; deleting source material must offer to delete what was derived from it; complete deletion means removing the vault directory because nothing personal lives outside it. Raw audio and screenshots are never written in Phase 0 because no such subsystem exists.

nodes.label: Export and Import Constraints
nodes.rationale: Normal exports exclude API keys, cookies, login sessions, OAuth refresh tokens, passwords, private keys and device-specific absolute paths; secrets may only leave through a separate passphrase-protected encrypted export after an explicit warning. Audit log, screenshots, browser profile, file index, app logs, runtime_instance and resource_lock are never exported by default.

nodes.label: SQLite Concurrency Strategy (WAL, per-thread connections)
nodes.rationale: WAL allows concurrent readers alongside the scheduler's writer; one connection per thread because sqlite3 connections are not shareable; BEGIN IMMEDIATE for writes so a conflict fails fast rather than deadlocking mid-transaction; lock acquisition is a single transaction so partial acquisition is impossible; WAL checkpoint on shutdown so the .db file is complete and backup-safe.

nodes.label: Ten Persisted Integrity Invariants
nodes.rationale: Test-covered: user_version matches SCHEMA_VERSION, every grant's capability exists, no grant for a prohibited capability, no non-once standing allow for high risk, valid task states and legal transitions, one lock row per name, declared failure codes only, audit row count matches audit.jsonl line count, and no secret-shaped value anywhere in audit.jsonl.

nodes.label: Entities Defined But Not Yet Built
nodes.rationale: Conversation, memory, skill, schedule, clipboard, notification, document and screenshot entities arrive with the capability that needs them, because declaring a table before anything writes to it would be speculative schema.
nodes.norm_label: entities defined but not yet built

nodes.label: Project Jarvis (local-first Windows desktop AI agent)
nodes.rationale: Jarvis is an internal codename only and is not the public product name (PRD 1.16, ADR-0011).
nodes.norm_label: project jarvis (local-first windows desktop ai agent)

nodes.label: Phase 0 Scope Statement
nodes.rationale: No voice input or output, no desktop or browser automation, no filesystem tools, no screen capture and no clipboard access. What exists is the machinery those capabilities will have to pass through.

nodes.label: CLI Flags (--check, --data-dir, --log-level, --allow-multiple-instances)
nodes.rationale: --check starts the core, prints a status report and exits with no GUI; --allow-multiple-instances is development only and skips the single-instance guard.

nodes.label: How to Add a Capability
nodes.rationale: Write a narrow typed tool in jarvis/toolbox/, declare its capability in the catalogue with a risk level and register it. There is no generic execution path, and adding one fails the build.

nodes.label: No Bundled Third-Party Assets
nodes.rationale: Pre-release, not for redistribution. No third-party models, voices, icons or copyrighted assets are bundled; tray icons are drawn programmatically for exactly this reason (PRD 17.3).

nodes.label: Release 0.1.0.dev0 - Phase 0 Foundation and Safety Architecture
nodes.rationale: The foundation every later capability has to pass through, shipped with no computer-control features. Keep a Changelog format, Semantic Versioning.
nodes.norm_label: release 0.1.0.dev0 - phase 0 foundation and safety architecture

nodes.label: Phase 0 Known Limitations
nodes.rationale: No approval dialog exists, so only capabilities with a standing grant can run - two self-inspection capabilities receive a visible revocable bootstrap grant at first start. In-process isolation is not a security boundary. A timed-out tool is abandoned, not killed, because Python cannot forcibly stop a thread, so the tool's own timeout remains the primary defence. Secret storage is deferred to Phase 1 when the first secret exists.

nodes.label: system.health (the one registered Phase 0 tool)
nodes.rationale: Read-only, routed through the full invoker pipeline, proving the pipeline end to end without granting any computer-control capability.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Enforcement of the No-Shell Rule
nodes.rationale: No shell, Command Prompt, PowerShell, WSL or arbitrary-code execution exists anywhere in the runtime, enforced in three layers (ADR-0003): registry identity denylist, name-pattern denylist, and an AST scan of the package in CI.
nodes.norm_label: three-layer enforcement of the no-shell rule

nodes.label: Target Hardware Profile
nodes.rationale: NVIDIA RTX 5070 12GB, AMD Ryzen 9 7900X, 32GB RAM, 1TB SSD on Windows 11 x64 - the constraint behind quantised 8-9B models and sequential model loading.

nodes.label: Selected Model Stack (planner, vision, embeddings)
nodes.rationale: qwen3.5:9b-q4_K_M for planning, qwen3-vl:8b-instruct-q4_K_M for vision, qwen3-embedding:0.6b for embeddings - all quantised to fit 12GB VRAM.

nodes.label: Kokoro bm_george (default TTS provider)
nodes.rationale: hexgrad/Kokoro-82M, British English (language_code b), CPU device, speed 1.0, Python 3.11 - selected and verified.

nodes.label: Qwen3-TTS Expressive Provider (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice needs Python 3.12 and CUDA so it runs as an isolated worker, disabled by default pending benchmark. Activation policy: never switch voice silently, the user selects the active voice profile, benchmark before product activation.

nodes.label: Windows SAPI Fallback Voice
nodes.rationale: Always available OS-provided voice so speech output degrades honestly rather than disappearing.

nodes.label: faster-whisper Speech Recognition
nodes.rationale: small model, CPU, int8 compute, English, preloaded and kept loaded on startup, raw audio never retained. Original transcript is preserved.

nodes.label: Wake Word Policy (Hey Jarvis now, Jarvis desired)
nodes.rationale: Development phrase is 'Hey Jarvis'; the desired phrase is the single word 'Jarvis' (a custom wake word, ADR-0016). Push-to-talk is enabled but always-listening with wake-word activation is preferred.
nodes.norm_label: wake word policy (hey jarvis now, jarvis desired)

nodes.label: Rust Deferred Until After Phase 3
nodes.rationale: Version 1 is Python 3.11. Rust is reconsidered after Phase 3 and would scope to the native shell, tray, global hotkeys, updater and secure IPC - which is precisely why the architecture keeps cross-component messages typed and Qt out of the engine.

nodes.label: Privacy Defaults (telemetry off, no raw audio)
nodes.rationale: Default network mode local_assistant, telemetry disabled, raw audio retention disabled, screenshots task-only, permanent memory requires approval.
nodes.norm_label: privacy defaults (telemetry off, no raw audio)

nodes.label: Automation Safety Defaults
nodes.rationale: Administrator mode disabled, a dedicated browser profile named Jarvis, force-close and file-delete both require confirmation, emergency stop bound to Ctrl+Alt+Pause.

nodes.label: defaults.yaml schema_version pin
nodes.rationale: Every key in defaults.yaml must exist in jarvis.config.schema; unknown keys are a startup error, not a silently ignored value. Personal preferences belong in user.yaml which records only the difference (ADR-0006).

nodes.label: network.mode (offline / local_assistant / connected)
nodes.rationale: Default local_assistant: local model only, with network tools available when explicitly invoked. offline makes no network request from any component; connected enables optional configured search or cloud providers.

nodes.label: llm.ollama settings (loopback base_url, require_loopback)
nodes.rationale: base_url http://127.0.0.1:11434, 10s request timeout, 300s health-check interval, require_loopback true.

nodes.label: models.* role-to-profile mapping
nodes.rationale: planner, vision and embeddings each name a provider, model name and context length so nothing hard-codes a model.

nodes.label: model_runtime (sequential load strategy)
nodes.rationale: idle_unload_seconds 180, load_strategy sequential, allow_parallel_heavy_models false - the configuration-only stub for the resource scheduler that prevents two heavy models loading at once on 12GB VRAM.

nodes.label: audio.text_to_speech profiles
nodes.rationale: Three named profiles - kokoro_bm_george (active), qwen3_tts_expressive (isolated_worker, disabled, experimental) and windows_sapi (fallback_only) - so switching voices is a configuration choice the user makes explicitly.

nodes.label: audio.speech_to_text settings
nodes.rationale: faster_whisper small on CPU with int8, VAD filter on, beam_size 1, preloaded and warmed at startup with idle_unload_seconds 0, retain_raw_audio false.

nodes.label: audio.wake_word settings
nodes.rationale: openwakeword provider, phrase 'Hey Jarvis', push-to-talk enabled.

nodes.label: permissions.default_policy
nodes.rationale: Fallback decision per risk level when no grant matches; all three default to ask. High risk is always ask and cannot be configured otherwise (PRD 11.1). session_grant_ttl_seconds 3600, allow_always_for_low_risk true.

nodes.label: tasks scheduler settings
nodes.rationale: max_concurrent 2, default_max_retries 3, lock_acquire_timeout_seconds 0.0 (fail fast rather than block), poll interval 0.1s, step timeout 120s.

nodes.label: logging settings (audit_to_sqlite, max_audit_value_chars)
nodes.rationale: max_audit_value_chars 512 is the truncation bound that stops a log entry being used to smuggle out a document.

nodes.label: ui settings (tray start, show_unavailable_features, emergency hotkey)
nodes.rationale: show_unavailable_features true is the configuration expression of the honest-degraded-UI decision; emergency_stop_hotkey is Ctrl+Alt+Pause.
nodes.norm_label: ui settings (tray start, show_unavailable_features, emergency hotkey)

nodes.label: storage paths (huggingface_home, application_data, workspace)
nodes.rationale: Windows environment variables are written as %LOCALAPPDATA% / %USERPROFILE% literals and expanded only by VaultPaths.

nodes.label: privacy retention defaults
nodes.rationale: raw_audio_retention disabled, generated_voice_retention temporary, screenshot_retention task_only, telemetry_enabled false.

nodes.label: CI test job (Windows + Ubuntu, Python 3.11/3.12)
nodes.rationale: Windows is the product target; Ubuntu runs too because the engine must stay importable and testable without Windows-only APIs - a regression there means the layering has been broken.

nodes.label: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen in CI
nodes.rationale: No test may touch a real user profile, and Qt has no display in CI, so the UI suite runs headless.

nodes.label: CI headless self-check step (jarvis.main --check)
nodes.rationale: Runs python -m jarvis.main --check against a temporary data dir, proving the whole core starts with no Qt and no real vault.

nodes.label: CI security-invariants job
nodes.rationale: tests/security runs as its own job so a broken invariant is unmistakable in the job list rather than buried in a long test log (ADR-0003).

nodes.label: CI dependency and licence review job
nodes.rationale: pip-audit --strict is advisory (continue-on-error) for now and becomes blocking before the first public build (ADR-0026); pip-licenses produces the licence inventory required by PRD NFR-023.
nodes.norm_label: ci dependency and licence review job

nodes.label: Project Jarvis Implementation Backlog
nodes.rationale: Exists so the phased execution plan can be tracked, reviewed and re-planned without re-deriving intent from the PRD each time; deliberately adds no scope the PRD does not contain and refuses calendar-time estimates.

nodes.label: THREAT_MODEL.md
nodes.rationale: Named as a Phase 0 deliverable but does not yet exist; the per-phase gate that re-reviews it cannot execute until it is written, so its absence blocks the Phase 0 gate rather than being mere documentation debt.

nodes.label: PROJECT_INPUTS.md working defaults
nodes.rationale: Holds provisional resolutions (Kokoro bm_george voice, faster-whisper small, 'Hey Jarvis' development wake phrase, screenshot_retention: task_only) for PRD open decisions that have no ADR yet, so work can proceed without pretending the decisions are final.

nodes.label: Work item ID scheme P<phase>-<area>-<nn>
nodes.rationale: Sequence numbers are unique within phase+area and deliberately do NOT imply execution order — only the 'Depends on' column does — so items can be renumbered or added without implying a schedule.

nodes.label: Subsystem area codes (CFG, COR, SEC, TSK, AUD, LLM, ...)
nodes.rationale: Three-letter codes map each work item onto exactly one subsystem and one PRD section range, which is what makes the §10 requirement coverage matrix checkable.
nodes.norm_label: subsystem area codes (cfg, cor, sec, tsk, aud, llm, ...)

nodes.label: S/M/L/XL effort sizing (not time)
nodes.rationale: The PRD forbids fabricated calendar estimates (§9.6, §27), so sizing expresses scope of collaboration and test surface instead: XL explicitly means 'expected to be split into sub-tasks during execution'.

nodes.label: Cross-phase invariants
nodes.rationale: Restated once rather than per-item because they apply to every work item in every phase; phases repeat them only where they add a concrete enforcement mechanism.

nodes.label: Invariant: every item ships with tests
nodes.rationale: A feature with no test is not a completed backlog item regardless of whether it demos — demo-ability is explicitly rejected as evidence of completion.
nodes.norm_label: invariant: every item ships with tests

nodes.label: Invariant: no generic execution primitive
nodes.rationale: Enforced structurally rather than by review discipline: any shell/interpreter/'do anything' tool name or call site fails tests/security/test_no_shell.py and the tool-registry denylist, so the property cannot erode through inattention.

nodes.label: Invariant: state-changing tools declare reversibility metadata
nodes.rationale: The field lives on ToolSpec from Phase 0 so reversibility, rollback method, expiry and required approval are declared at registration time and cannot be retrofitted after tools exist.
nodes.norm_label: invariant: state-changing tools declare reversibility metadata

nodes.label: Invariant: every phase gate re-reviews THREAT_MODEL.md
nodes.rationale: Each phase adds new attack surface (new content source, automation target, external process); re-reading the threat model against what was actually built forces that surface to be covered or recorded as an open risk.
nodes.norm_label: invariant: every phase gate re-reviews threat_model.md

nodes.label: Invariant: phase exit criteria must be demonstrated
nodes.rationale: Not implemented, not merged — demonstrated, with an acceptance test or recorded manual walkthrough tied to the specific exit-criterion sentence, which is why each phase reproduces PRD §21 verbatim as a checklist.
nodes.norm_label: invariant: phase exit criteria must be demonstrated

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Foundation and safety architecture
nodes.rationale: Exists specifically so 'no generic execution primitive' and 'every action is auditable' are structural properties of the codebase before any feature that could misuse them exists; ships a tray-and-window shell with no computer-control capability behind it at all.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Voice-first local assistant
nodes.rationale: Wires the audio stack to the Ollama-hosted model and closes the two Phase 0 gaps that block real interaction (approval dialog UI, protected secret store); performs no desktop or browser automation beyond opening an approved application or URL.

nodes.label: Phase 2 — Deterministic desktop and browser automation
nodes.rationale: UI Automation before coordinates, DOM selectors before pixels, foreground lock before anything moves. Mutating filesystem operations are deliberately deferred to Phase 3 so undo and recovery exist to back them first.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 — deterministic desktop and browser automation

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Tasks, macros, and memory
nodes.rationale: Matures the task engine from substrate into a user-facing system and introduces every state-changing filesystem operation deliberately alongside undo, recovery and reversibility rather than before them.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — Vision fallback and long-running workflows
nodes.rationale: Vision is a fallback of last resort, used only when UI Automation and DOM access are insufficient; this is also the first phase where genuinely heterogeneous concurrent tasks compete for locks.
nodes.norm_label: phase 4 — vision fallback and long-running workflows

nodes.label: Phase 5 — IDE orchestration
nodes.rationale: Deliberately the smallest phase: PRD §26 'Ruthless Scope Guidance' says reliable narrow coverage beats broad unreliable coverage, and IDE orchestration is the PRD's own example of a single deep integration rather than a platform.

nodes.label: Phase 6 — Productisation
nodes.rationale: Adds no new automation capability; it makes every capability from Phases 0-5 discoverable, configurable and safe to hand to someone else's machine.

nodes.label: ToolInvoker
nodes.rationale: The single approval choke point: everything destructive, including IDE-agent proposals, routes back through the same ToolInvoker path as every other high-risk action.

nodes.label: LockManager
nodes.rationale: Gets its first real multi-task exercise only in Phase 4, when heterogeneous concurrent tasks first compete for the same resources.

nodes.label: P0-CFG-03 SQLite storage and versioned forward migrations
nodes.rationale: A database newer than the running binary is a hard startup failure (NFR-043) rather than a best-effort read, so downgrades cannot silently corrupt the vault.
nodes.norm_label: p0-cfg-03 sqlite storage and versioned forward migrations

nodes.label: P0-COR-02 Tool contract: ToolSpec with reversibility metadata
nodes.norm_label: p0-cor-02 tool contract: toolspec with reversibility metadata

nodes.label: P0-COR-03 Tool registry with identity and pattern denylist
nodes.rationale: Denies by pattern as well as identity so invented variants such as run_shell_v2 are rejected without anyone having to enumerate them first.
nodes.norm_label: p0-cor-03 tool registry with identity and pattern denylist

nodes.label: P0-COR-04 Tool invoker six-step pipeline
nodes.rationale: Allow-list, schema, permission, locks, approval, execute — a fixed ordered pipeline so no call site can reach execution without passing every gate.

nodes.label: P0-SEC-01 Audit log with redaction (JSONL + SQLite dual sink)
nodes.norm_label: p0-sec-01 audit log with redaction (jsonl + sqlite dual sink)

nodes.label: P0-SEC-03 Permission engine
nodes.rationale: ALWAYS grants are structurally rejected for HIGH/PROHIBITED risk, so a convenience setting can never silently pre-authorise a destructive capability.

nodes.label: P0-TSK-03 Resource locks (named, exclusive, persisted)
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing acquisition over a sorted lock set prevents deadlock; stale reclamation on startup prevents a dead instance from permanently holding the foreground.

nodes.label: P0-LLM-01 Ollama health check (loopback-only, offline-aware)
nodes.rationale: In offline mode the checker returns skipped(reason='offline_mode') without opening a socket, which is what makes AT-001 executable rather than a claim.

nodes.label: P0-UI-01 PySide6 tray and main window shell
nodes.norm_label: p0-ui-01 pyside6 tray and main window shell

nodes.label: P1-AUD-01 Wake-word detection (openWakeWord)
nodes.rationale: The development phrase is 'Hey Jarvis'; bare 'Jarvis' is desired but unproven, and FR-011 forbids the GUI from promising reliability it has not earned.

nodes.label: P1-AUD-10 Expressive TTS worker isolation prototype (Qwen3-TTS)
nodes.rationale: First cross-Python-version process boundary in the product (Python 3.12, typed authenticated IPC); disabled by default and given its own focused test pass before Phase 4 adds a second GPU-resident model alongside it.
nodes.norm_label: p1-aud-10 expressive tts worker isolation prototype (qwen3-tts)

nodes.label: P1-LLM-01 Ollama conversational model, structured tool-call output only
nodes.rationale: Free text never reaches the invoker — only a structured tool-call schema does, which keeps model output from becoming an execution channel.
nodes.norm_label: p1-llm-01 ollama conversational model, structured tool-call output only

nodes.label: P1-APP-01 Application launcher with launch verification
nodes.norm_label: p1-app-01 application launcher with launch verification

nodes.label: P1-SEC-01 Approval dialog UI replacing DenyingApprovalPort
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 intentionally shipped DenyingApprovalPort as the default so nothing requiring ASK could run at all; the real dialog is the first Phase 1 deliverable rather than a Phase 0 shortcut.
nodes.norm_label: p1-sec-01 approval dialog ui replacing denyingapprovalport

nodes.label: P2-WIN-03 Automation worker thread (pywinauto UIA backend)
nodes.rationale: This is where in-process isolation stops being theoretical: the automation worker now does real things, and a defect in it can reach the vault until process separation lands.
nodes.norm_label: p2-win-03 automation worker thread (pywinauto uia backend)

nodes.label: P2-WIN-04 Input ownership via foreground_desktop lock
nodes.norm_label: p2-win-04 input ownership via foreground_desktop lock

nodes.label: P2-WIN-05 User-interruption pause on mouse/keyboard activity
nodes.norm_label: p2-win-05 user-interruption pause on mouse/keyboard activity

nodes.label: P2-BRW-01 Dedicated persistent Jarvis Brave profile
nodes.norm_label: p2-brw-01 dedicated persistent jarvis brave profile

nodes.label: P2-BRW-06 Untrusted web-content wrapping and prompt-injection test
nodes.rationale: First point where untrusted content reaches the planner; the delimiter strategy was 'specified but unexercised' until here, making AT-007 load-bearing for the whole product's safety story rather than routine coverage.
nodes.norm_label: p2-brw-06 untrusted web-content wrapping and prompt-injection test

nodes.label: P2-BRW-08 YouTube search and indexed result selection
nodes.norm_label: p2-brw-08 youtube search and indexed result selection

nodes.label: P2-FS-06 Filesystem scoping and path validation
nodes.rationale: Path resolution must reject traversal via symlink, junction, or '..' outside the approved root — the boundary is enforced after resolution, not on the raw string.
nodes.norm_label: p2-fs-06 filesystem scoping and path validation

nodes.label: P3-TSK-02 Pause/resume with mandatory state re-observation
nodes.rationale: Resume re-observes rather than trusting the checkpoint, because the desktop may have changed while the task was paused.
nodes.norm_label: p3-tsk-02 pause/resume with mandatory state re-observation

nodes.label: P3-SKL-01 Macro recorder with semantic capture priority order
nodes.rationale: Largest item by dependency count: needs both UIA and browser backends to capture semantically. Its fallback order (UIA element to browser selector to keyboard shortcut to mouse action to coordinate anchor) is flagged as the kind of logic that looks done on the happy path and breaks on the first real application.
nodes.norm_label: p3-skl-01 macro recorder with semantic capture priority order

nodes.label: P3-MEM-01 Memory candidate pipeline with review queue and provenance
nodes.norm_label: p3-mem-01 memory candidate pipeline with review queue and provenance

nodes.label: P3-MEM-03 Forget with cascade delete from derived indexes
nodes.rationale: Deletion must remove the memory from retrieval and every derived index in the same transaction, otherwise a 'deleted' memory keeps surfacing through an embedding index.
nodes.norm_label: p3-mem-03 forget with cascade delete from derived indexes

nodes.label: P3-MEM-06 Portable identity export/import (.jarvispack) with secret exclusion
nodes.rationale: Round-trip preserves personality, memories, skills and aliases while containing no keys, cookies, tokens or credentials — portability of identity is explicitly separated from portability of authority.
nodes.norm_label: p3-mem-06 portable identity export/import (.jarvispack) with secret exclusion

nodes.label: P3-FS-02 File create/copy/move/rename with boundary-crossing approval
nodes.norm_label: p3-fs-02 file create/copy/move/rename with boundary-crossing approval

nodes.label: P3-FS-04 Undo command and end-to-end reversibility
nodes.rationale: Depends on reversibility metadata declared in Phase 0 but never exercised against a real rollback until now; the backlog explicitly expects the first genuine design gaps in that metadata to surface here.
nodes.norm_label: p3-fs-04 undo command and end-to-end reversibility

nodes.label: P4-LLM-01 Model resource scheduler (sequential loading, VRAM checks)
nodes.rationale: FR-039 is legitimately two-phase: configuration-only in Phase 1 because the scheduler cannot prevent unsafe simultaneous loading of a vision model that does not exist until Phase 4.
nodes.norm_label: p4-llm-01 model resource scheduler (sequential loading, vram checks)

nodes.label: P4-VIS-02 Screenshot grounding and UIA-plus-vision fusion
nodes.rationale: Coordinate-only actions are explicitly marked fragile rather than treated as equivalent to element-addressed ones.
nodes.norm_label: p4-vis-02 screenshot grounding and uia-plus-vision fusion

nodes.label: P4-VIS-03 Vision action verification
nodes.rationale: Timestamp, proposed target, confidence, bounds and a post-action check are the control that makes the phase's 'every visual click is verified' exit criterion true rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: P4-TSK-04 Heterogeneous concurrent resource locking
nodes.rationale: AT-009 is only partially demonstrable in Phase 2 (two instances of the same tool); full demonstration needs genuinely different task types and so becomes a Phase 4 exit criterion.

nodes.label: P4-FS-01 Document processing core
nodes.rationale: Unsupported formats return an explicit explanation, never fabricated content.

nodes.label: P4-WIN-05 Security-settings boundary and scoped elevation helper
nodes.rationale: First plausible consumer of an elevated helper process; FR-004 is attached here by the backlog's own judgement, not by PRD instruction, and ADR-0009 should be resolved before the item starts rather than discovered mid-implementation.
nodes.norm_label: p4-win-05 security-settings boundary and scoped elevation helper

nodes.label: P5-IDE-01 Antigravity adapter: launch and open
nodes.rationale: Treated as another UI-Automation-first integration, not a special case, so it inherits Phase 2's answer to coordinate/DOM fragility instead of inventing a new one.
nodes.norm_label: p5-ide-01 antigravity adapter: launch and open

nodes.label: P5-IDE-05 IDE permission boundary (no automatic approval)
nodes.norm_label: p5-ide-05 ide permission boundary (no automatic approval)

nodes.label: P5-IDE-08 No hidden shell delegation (adversarial test)
nodes.rationale: An agentic IDE is by construction a tool that can execute code, so the boundary Jarvis owns is what it will ASK the IDE to do and what it will AUTO-APPROVE on the IDE's behalf; the test must try to smuggle a prohibited action through the IDE prompt, not merely inspect the adapter's tool list.
nodes.norm_label: p5-ide-08 no hidden shell delegation (adversarial test)

nodes.label: P6-PKG-03 Signed Windows x64 installer
nodes.rationale: Blocked on PRD open decisions #1, #3, #12 and #16, none of which has a working default in PROJECT_INPUTS.md the way the model and voice choices do.

nodes.label: P6-PKG-08 Plugin/adapter SDK groundwork
nodes.rationale: Deliberately scoped as groundwork and interface stability, not a third-party plugin ecosystem, because PRD open decision #13 (in-process vs isolated plugins) is unresolved.

nodes.label: tests/security/test_no_shell.py
nodes.rationale: Fails the build on subprocess, os.system, os.popen, eval(, exec(, shell=True, ShellExecute or CreateProcess anywhere in src/ — a build-time property rather than a runtime check.

nodes.label: tests/security/test_prompt_injection.py
nodes.rationale: A fixture page containing 'ignore previous instructions' / 'click Allow' must be logged as untrusted content and never treated as authority.

nodes.label: PRD §6 non-goals (permanent constraints)
nodes.rationale: These twelve items are not backlog work deferred to a later phase; they are constraints every phase already respects, restated only so nobody re-schedules them as future features.

nodes.label: Deferred beyond Version 1
nodes.rationale: Process separation and the native shell are trigger-based rather than scheduled; multiple simultaneous foreground-control tasks are explicitly NOT a temporary limitation to lift later but a permanent architectural constraint (PRD §7.1, non-goal #11).

nodes.label: ADR-0001 Python-first shell (native Rust/Tauri deferred)
nodes.rationale: Reconsidered only after Phase 3 and only if a measured requirement (startup latency, idle memory, packaging reliability, crash isolation, update requirements, Windows integration limits) cannot reasonably be met in Python — not adopted for theoretical performance alone.

nodes.label: ADR-0009 Scoped elevation helper interface
nodes.rationale: If no Phase 0-6 feature genuinely requires elevation, FR-004's mechanism may stay interface-only through Version 1 — but that must be recorded as a deliberate ADR-backed scope decision, not discovered as a silent gap at Phase 6 sign-off.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Python-First Implementation with Rust Deferred
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001: python-first implementation with rust deferred

nodes.label: Python 3.11 + PySide6 Implementation Stack
nodes.rationale: The selected AI, speech, browser automation and Windows automation stack has strong first-class Python support; rewriting these integrations in Rust would increase development and packaging complexity without materially reducing model-inference latency.

nodes.label: Rust/Tauri Native Shell Deferred Past Phase 3
nodes.rationale: Rust or Tauri may replace the native shell only after Phase 3 and only if performance or distribution measurements justify it; no migration begins without measured acceptance criteria.
nodes.norm_label: rust/tauri native shell deferred past phase 3

nodes.label: Qwen3-TTS Isolated Python 3.12 Worker
nodes.rationale: Requires Python 3.12 and CUDA, a dependency set conflicting with the Python 3.11 host, so it must be a separate process regardless of general policy.

nodes.label: Authenticated Typed IPC for Future Shell
nodes.rationale: Core interfaces remain typed and process-compatible so a future Rust shell can communicate through authenticated typed IPC without an interface redesign.
nodes.norm_label: authenticated typed ipc for future shell

nodes.label: ADR-0002: SQLite as the Single Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: sqlite as the single source of truth

nodes.label: SQLite (jarvis.db) Canonical Transactional Store
nodes.rationale: One transactional writer with ACID guarantees, embedded and zero-install; spreading canonical facts across independent stores or mixing the record of what happened with a rebuildable search structure leads to silent disagreement between them.

nodes.label: WAL Mode Concurrent Readers
nodes.rationale: WAL gives concurrent readers (GUI, audit viewer) alongside the scheduler's single writer, matching the actual access pattern.

nodes.label: One SQLite Connection Per Thread
nodes.rationale: SQLite connections are not shared across threads; each thread that touches the database owns its own connection, avoiding lock contention under a serialised writer.

nodes.label: Derived Rebuildable Stores Hold No Unique Information
nodes.rationale: Embedding index, file index and caches exist purely as accelerators; losing them must never lose data, only rebuild time. Any new store that would hold unreconstructable information violates this ADR.
nodes.norm_label: derived rebuildable stores hold no unique information

nodes.label: Large Binary Artefacts Stored on Disk, Referenced by Path
nodes.rationale: Screenshots, audio diagnostics and evidence live on disk rather than as BLOBs, keeping the database small and fast to back up.
nodes.norm_label: large binary artefacts stored on disk, referenced by path

nodes.label: Versioned Forward-Only Migrations
nodes.rationale: No down-migration path in Version 1; recovery from a bad migration is restore-from-backup, not a rollback script. Hand-written migrations are easier to security-review than ORM-generated ones.

nodes.label: Schema-Version Startup Check (Newer DB is Hard Failure)
nodes.rationale: Runs first in JarvisCore.start(), before the event bus or audit log is constructed; a database newer than the binary aborts startup rather than attempting a best-effort open.
nodes.norm_label: schema-version startup check (newer db is hard failure)

nodes.label: Full ORM (SQLAlchemy) Rejected for Phase 0
nodes.rationale: An ORM's session/identity-map semantics add implicit behaviour on top of a safety-critical store; audit events must never silently merge or be deduplicated by an identity map.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: A Closed Capability Set — No Generic Execution Primitive
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: a closed capability set — no generic execution primitive

nodes.label: Closed Enumerated Set of Narrow Typed Tools
nodes.rationale: The blast radius of any single tool is bounded and reviewable in isolation; a reviewer can read the full list of things Jarvis can possibly do in one sitting. Feature velocity is deliberately traded for boundedness.
nodes.norm_label: closed enumerated set of narrow typed tools

nodes.label: No Generic Execution Primitive
nodes.rationale: A locally-running agent reachable by voice or compromised prompt with a general-purpose way to execute code is a remote-code-execution primitive with a friendly voice. No shell, PowerShell, cmd, WSL, subprocess, eval or exec exists anywhere in the runtime.

nodes.label: Sandboxed Generic Shell Rejected
nodes.rationale: A restricted-command allow-list inside a shell is a closed capability set again, implemented as string matching instead of typed signatures — strictly worse, because quoting, environment expansion and && chaining are easier to smuggle past than a schema validator.

nodes.label: Tool Registry Identity and Pattern Denylist
nodes.rationale: Rejects registration two ways — exact denylisted identity and name pattern — so a contributor cannot dodge the identity check by registering run_shell_v2 or shell_helper.
nodes.norm_label: tool registry identity and pattern denylist

nodes.label: tests/security/test_no_shell.py Source Tree Scan
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing enforcement layer: scans all of src/ for subprocess, os.system, os.popen, eval(, exec(, shell=True, ShellExecute, CreateProcess and fails the build even for unreachable code, because 'not currently wired up' is not a safety property worth relying on.

nodes.label: ToolSpec Typed Tool Contract
nodes.rationale: Every tool declares a risk category, permission requirement, resource-lock set and verification method, giving the permission engine and audit log something concrete to reason about.

nodes.label: Hard Ceiling on Prompt Injection Impact
nodes.rationale: Injected text can at most cause a legitimate tool to be proposed with attacker-chosen parameters; it can never grant a new category of action that does not already exist as a reviewed tool.
nodes.norm_label: hard ceiling on prompt injection impact

nodes.label: Emergent Capability From Tool Composition (Residual Risk)
nodes.rationale: A sufficiently large permitted tool set could in combination approximate a shell; each tool is reviewed individually but the composition is not formally analysed — a standing review responsibility, not a solved problem.
nodes.norm_label: emergent capability from tool composition (residual risk)

nodes.label: os.startfile Named Future Allow-Listed Exception
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 needs os.startfile to launch approved applications; it must arrive as a single reviewed allow-listed call site in a follow-up ADR, never by weakening the test_no_shell.py scan or broadening its exception list.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: Single Process, Thread Isolation for Phases 0–3
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: single process, thread isolation for phases 0–3

nodes.label: Single Process with Worker Threads (Phases 0–3)
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 has no audio, automation or elevation to isolate yet; imposing process separation now would pay IPC authentication, token rotation and supervision cost before there is anything concrete to protect, against interfaces still being discovered.

nodes.label: Layering Rule: Core Packages Must Not Import PySide6
nodes.rationale: jarvis.core, jarvis.tasks, jarvis.storage, jarvis.llm and jarvis.config must not import PySide6, keeping the engine headlessly testable and the GUI a replaceable adapter — the same property a real process boundary would give, achieved by import discipline instead.
nodes.norm_label: layering rule: core packages must not import pyside6

nodes.label: tests/security/test_layering.py Import Discipline Test
nodes.rationale: Asserts the layering table holds and that jarvis.ui is the only package permitted to import PySide6; any new import outside jarvis.ui fails this test.

nodes.label: Thread Isolation Is Not a Security Boundary (Gap 2)
nodes.rationale: In Phases 0–3 a defect in the automation worker can reach the vault, because both run as threads in the same process with the same memory and filesystem access. Deferred, not solved — which is why the closed capability set and permission engine matter as much as they do.
nodes.norm_label: thread isolation is not a security boundary (gap 2)

nodes.label: Process-Separation Promotion Triggers
nodes.rationale: Qwen3-TTS worker (conflicting Python 3.12/CUDA dependency set), the elevated action helper, any adapter with a conflicting dependency set, and a scheduled Phase 3 review.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: An In-Process Typed Event Bus
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: an in-process typed event bus

nodes.label: jarvis.core.events In-Process Publish/Subscribe Bus
nodes.rationale: A same-process cross-thread notification problem solved with the smallest mechanism that fits, not one borrowed from a different scale of system. Deliberately not a message broker: no persistence, no retry, no cross-thread ordering guarantee.

nodes.label: Frozen Pydantic Event Models with Subclass Matching
nodes.rationale: Every event derives from a common Event base carrying event_id, occurred_at and source; subscribers match by subclass, so no routing-key convention has to be kept in sync.
nodes.norm_label: frozen pydantic event models with subclass matching

nodes.label: Per-Handler Exception Isolation
nodes.rationale: A raising handler is caught, logged and isolated — the audit log and GUI bridge are both subscribers and a defect in one must never silence the other. Isolation covers exceptions, not latency.

nodes.label: jarvis.ui.qt_bridge.EventBridge
nodes.rationale: Subscribes once on behalf of the whole UI layer and re-emits every event as a queued Qt signal — the single place where the domain's any-thread-may-publish model and Qt's main-thread-only model meet.

nodes.label: Qt Signals/Slots Throughout Rejected
nodes.rationale: Would require jarvis.core and every capability module to import PySide6, directly violating ADR-0004's layering rule; it couples the domain model to a specific GUI toolkit for no benefit the toolkit provides here.

nodes.label: Bus Is Notification, Not System of Record
nodes.rationale: Anything needing durability goes through the task store and audit log directly; publishing durable state through the bus alone with no corresponding row in jarvis.db violates ADR-0002 and is a bug, not a design choice.
nodes.norm_label: bus is notification, not system of record

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Layered Configuration with Override-Only Persistence
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006: layered configuration with override-only persistence

nodes.label: Three-Layer Config Merge (defaults.yaml, user.yaml, JARVIS_* env)
nodes.rationale: Merged deepest-first then validated into one frozen pydantic AppConfig tree; a single flat settings file either clobbers user edits on new defaults or lets untouched defaults go stale.
nodes.norm_label: three-layer config merge (defaults.yaml, user.yaml, jarvis_* env)

nodes.label: Override-Only Persistence (Delta from Defaults)
nodes.rationale: Shipping a new default changes behaviour for every setting the user has not touched and never silently reverts one they explicitly chose — the two properties a whole-file persistence design cannot deliver simultaneously.

nodes.label: pydantic extra="forbid" Loud Typo Failure
nodes.rationale: A typo in a settings key becomes a precise startup error naming the offending path, not a value silently dropped. It is itself the enforcement mechanism — there is no separate check to circumvent. Catches unknown keys, not semantically stale ones.

nodes.label: Atomic Config Write (Temp File + Rename)
nodes.rationale: A crash mid-save cannot leave user.yaml half-written and unparseable on the next launch.

nodes.label: jarvis.config.paths.VaultPaths
nodes.rationale: The single place Windows %LOCALAPPDATA% and %USERPROFILE% expansion happens; a second expansion site would create an inconsistent place where vault location logic could diverge.

nodes.label: JARVIS_DATA_DIR Vault Relocation and Test Isolation
nodes.rationale: One environment variable implements both the user-facing vault relocation requirement and per-test isolation, so relocation is exercised constantly in CI rather than being a rarely-tested GUI feature.
nodes.norm_label: jarvis_data_dir vault relocation and test isolation

nodes.label: ConfigChanged Runtime Event
nodes.rationale: Changing a setting at runtime publishes ConfigChanged on the event bus so components react to the new value rather than re-reading configuration defensively on every use.

nodes.label: Windows Registry Configuration Rejected
nodes.rationale: Not human-readable or diffable, harder to include in an export package, awkward to unit test without a real registry hive, and outside the spirit of a local-first, fully exportable product.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Base URL Enforcement at the Adapter
nodes.rationale: Refusing to open a connection to a non-loopback host closes the 'silently remote' failure mode structurally, so a misconfigured or tampered base URL cannot ship every prompt off the machine; the refusal is audited.
nodes.norm_label: loopback-only base url enforcement at the adapter

nodes.label: Offline Mode Enforced at the Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: In offline mode no socket is opened at all; the call returns skipped(reason="offline_mode"). This makes AT-001 a property of the adapter rather than an emergent property of every caller behaving correctly — distributed responsibility tends to have one forgotten call site.
nodes.norm_label: offline mode enforced at the adapter boundary

nodes.label: All Model Output Treated as Untrusted Input
nodes.rationale: The loopback restriction reduces who could plausibly be answering; it does not upgrade the trust level of what they say. Output must still pass the full invoker pipeline before it can have any effect.
nodes.norm_label: all model output treated as untrusted input

nodes.label: Six-Step Tool Invoker Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Schema validation, permission evaluation, resource-lock evaluation, tool allow-list validation, parameter validation, and approval where required. There is no code path from model text to action taken that skips the invoker.

nodes.label: Ollama Endpoint Squatting (Unmitigated Residual Risk)
nodes.rationale: Ollama's local HTTP API is unauthenticated by design; a rogue local process could squat the port and return malicious tool-call proposals. Version 1's only mitigation is that everything such a response proposes is still permission-, lock- and schema-checked by the invoker.

nodes.label: Local Authenticating Proxy for Ollama Not Adopted
nodes.rationale: Ollama's stock Windows distribution has no auth; patching it is fragile across updates and a proxy adds a process and attack surface of its own, for a threat (another process on the same user account) that already has substantial session access.
nodes.norm_label: local authenticating proxy for ollama not adopted

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Secret Storage Deferred to Phase 1
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: secret storage deferred to phase 1

nodes.label: No Secret Store Implemented in Phase 0
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 handles no secrets, so a store built now would be speculative security-critical code with no consumer to validate it against, liable to be wrong in ways that only surface once a real secret needed protecting. The absence of the capability is the absence of the risk.
nodes.norm_label: no secret store implemented in phase 0

nodes.label: DPAPI CryptProtectData via ctypes (Candidate Mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Ties encryption to the logged-in user's credentials with no separate key-management story; ctypes DATA_BLOB marshalling is unforgiving, and keys tied to the profile mean secrets do not migrate to a new machine without explicit re-entry.

nodes.label: Windows Credential Manager CredWrite/CredRead (Candidate Mechanism)
nodes.rationale: A purpose-built OS facility with an OS-native inspection UI, but a flat namespace with size limits and no room for per-secret metadata like expiry, scope or last-used.

nodes.label: Encrypted SQLite Table with DPAPI-Wrapped Key (Candidate Mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Keeps secrets in the canonical store with room for metadata, but a home-grown envelope-encryption scheme is easy to get subtly wrong (nonce reuse, key rotation, secure erasure) and duplicates protection Windows already offers natively.
nodes.norm_label: encrypted sqlite table with dpapi-wrapped key (candidate mechanism)

nodes.label: jarvis.core.audit.redaction Defence-in-Depth Backstop
nodes.rationale: Treats keys matching api_key, token, secret, password, credential as sensitive and value-pattern-matches high-entropy strings and PEM blocks, so an accidental secret in a tool parameter or log line is redacted before serialisation — a backstop, not a substitute for real secret storage.

nodes.label: Secrets Excluded From Normal Exports
nodes.rationale: The export pipeline must positively identify and skip secret-bearing entities, not merely happen not to include a table that does not exist yet; an optional passphrase-protected encrypted export may include them after explicit warning.

nodes.label: Secrets Never in Plaintext user.yaml
nodes.rationale: Fixing the constraint publicly now means Phase 1 cannot quietly ship a 'just put it in user.yaml for now' shortcut under time pressure; extra="forbid" would in any case reject an ad-hoc secret field.

nodes.label: ADR-0009: Scoped Elevation via a Separate Helper Process
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009: scoped elevation via a separate helper process

nodes.label: On-Demand Narrowly Scoped Elevated Helper Process
nodes.rationale: A separate process performs exactly one declared action, requested fresh each time, with the action displayed before Windows UAC appears; its bounded lifetime minimises the window during which anything runs elevated at all.
nodes.norm_label: on-demand narrowly scoped elevated helper process

nodes.label: Application Never Runs Permanently as Administrator
nodes.rationale: A persistent elevated service is 'runs as administrator all the time' wearing a service manifest, and any way to reach it from the unprivileged main process becomes a standing elevation-of-privilege path rather than one existing only for the seconds an approved action takes.
nodes.norm_label: application never runs permanently as administrator

nodes.label: No Interaction with the Windows Secure Desktop or UAC Prompt
nodes.rationale: The secure desktop exists so the process requesting elevation cannot control or spoof the consent prompt; any code path that would observe, screenshot or interact with it is a violation regardless of intent.
nodes.norm_label: no interaction with the windows secure desktop or uac prompt

nodes.label: Helper IPC Discipline (Named Pipe or Loopback, Rotating Token)
nodes.rationale: Bind only to loopback or a Windows named pipe, generate a per-installation authentication token, expose no unauthenticated network port, reject non-local interfaces, rotate the token during reset — applied to the highest-privilege component the product will ever run.
nodes.norm_label: helper ipc discipline (named pipe or loopback, rotating token)

nodes.label: No Elevation Manifest Security Check (asInvoker)
nodes.rationale: The security suite checks for the absence of an elevation manifest; its presence would be a direct signal the policy has been violated. Main process and single-instance guard both run asInvoker.

nodes.label: ADR-0010: Honest Degraded UI Over Fake Functionality
nodes.norm_label: adr-0010: honest degraded ui over fake functionality

nodes.label: Unavailable Features Shown Disabled with a Phase Tooltip
nodes.rationale: Showing the product's real shape makes phase progress observable (a nav item moving from disabled to enabled is direct evidence a phase landed); hiding features makes shipping a silent appearance, and a 'coming soon' toast is the same category of manufactured response as an unverified success message.
nodes.norm_label: unavailable features shown disabled with a phase tooltip

nodes.label: DenyingApprovalPort Default Implementation
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 has no approval dialog, so the default ApprovalPort refuses every request; any capability requiring ASK structurally cannot execute until a real port is wired in. Silence is never consent — the safe failure mode is the only failure mode.

nodes.label: ToolResult Distinguishes succeeded from unverified
nodes.rationale: A tool that cannot verify its own effect reports unverified and the task layer treats that as not-succeeded; there is no boolean 'worked' a tool can set to paper over the absence of real verification. Enforces the category distinction, not the quality of each tool's verification logic.

nodes.label: Programmatically Drawn QPainter Tray Icons
nodes.rationale: Rather than shipping placeholder artwork that risks quietly becoming the shipped product, the tray renders its seven states programmatically, which also sidesteps the third-party icon redistribution constraint until an original set exists.

nodes.label: Never Claim Unverified Success
nodes.rationale: 'I clicked it' is not equivalent to 'the task succeeded'; the standard has to hold everywhere a fake-success path could exist, not only in the tray, so 'success' means the same thing — verified — everywhere in the system.

nodes.label: "Jarvis" as Internal Codename Only
nodes.rationale: 'Jarvis'/'J.A.R.V.I.S.' is strongly associated with the Marvel/Iron Man franchise; a personal-AI-assistant product under that name invites plausible confusion. Internal use in source and docs is low risk — the risk crystallises at public distribution.

nodes.label: Rename Before Public Release (Leaning Option)
nodes.rationale: Lowest legal risk with no dependency on a legal-clearance timeline blocking release; a user's personal assistant can still be named Jarvis through the editable personality Name field without the product being marketed under it.

nodes.label: public_product_name Configuration Value
nodes.rationale: Keeping project_codename internal and rendering user-facing text from a distinct public_product_name value bounds the eventual rename to a small enumerable set of places rather than the whole codebase.

nodes.label: Trademark and Identifier Availability Criteria
nodes.rationale: A candidate must pass a US/EU availability screen in software/digital-assistant classes, have a free domain, installer AppId and MSIX Package Family Name, and not be confusingly similar to existing Store listings.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: Shell Technology for the First Public Build
nodes.norm_label: adr-0012: shell technology for the first public build

nodes.label: Python-Only PySide6 Shell (Status Quo, Extended)
nodes.rationale: Zero migration cost and fastest path to Phase 6, but interpreter/DLL startup overhead is real for an always-resident tray app, PyInstaller onedir builds have a larger footprint and slower cold start, and crash isolation stays weak.

nodes.label: Native .NET (WinUI 3 / WPF) Shell with Python Sidecars
nodes.rationale: Best Windows integration and structural crash isolation, and pairs naturally with MSIX where a small native front-end is easier to certify than a PyInstaller bundle — at the cost of two toolchains and every domain event crossing a real authenticated process boundary.
nodes.norm_label: native .net (winui 3 / wpf) shell with python sidecars

nodes.label: Rust/Tauri Shell with Python Sidecars
nodes.rationale: Smaller binary and lower memory than .NET and keeps the technology named in ADR-0001, but carries the same IPC-boundary rewrite cost without .NET's mature UIA, notification and Store-submission ecosystem.

nodes.label: Measurement-Driven Shell Decision Gate
nodes.rationale: Cold start to interactive tray, idle RSS with wake detection, clean-machine install success rate, whether crash isolation mattered in observed practice, hotkey and notification-action reliability, and an honest IPC-rewrite cost estimate. Rust shall not be adopted solely for theoretical performance.

nodes.label: EventBridge Discipline Keeps the Shell Decision Cheap to Defer
nodes.rationale: Every feature built directly against PySide6 signals rather than through the typed EventBridge increases the eventual IPC-boundary rewrite cost if a native shell is chosen later.
nodes.norm_label: eventbridge discipline keeps the shell decision cheap to defer

nodes.label: Inno Setup (Candidate Installer)
nodes.rationale: Straightforward per-user install with easy conditional prerequisite detection and large community precedent for the 'install an app, download large assets post-install' shape; code signing is a manual signtool step and repair is scripted rather than first-class.

nodes.label: WiX Toolset MSI (Candidate Installer)
nodes.rationale: Native OS repair/modify/uninstall semantics and an upgrade-code versioning model that maps cleanly onto preserving user data, but verbose XML authoring and per-user MSI rough edges that risk unwanted elevation prompts.

nodes.label: NSIS (Candidate Installer)
nodes.rationale: Very small installer binary and flexible scripting, but a more idiosyncratic language and a smaller ecosystem of maintained examples for the preserve-data/offer-deletion pattern.

nodes.label: Per-User Install with No UAC Elevation
nodes.rationale: Validates the non-administrator default at the install layer, not just at runtime; must be verified on a clean non-administrator Windows 11 account.
nodes.norm_label: per-user install with no uac elevation

nodes.label: Preserve Vault and user.yaml Across Updates
nodes.rationale: A correctness requirement, not a nice-to-have: the override-only config layering exists so upgrading changes only untouched settings, and an installer that does not honour it at the filesystem level would undermine that design. Repair must not touch jarvis.db or user.yaml, and the relocated-vault case must be handled.
nodes.norm_label: preserve vault and user.yaml across updates

nodes.label: Uninstall-Time Data Deletion Must Be Opt-In
nodes.rationale: The explicit data-deletion prompt at uninstall must never be a default action, to avoid an accidental destructive default.
nodes.norm_label: uninstall-time data deletion must be opt-in

nodes.label: Installer Choice Sequenced Behind the MSIX Decision
nodes.rationale: If MSIX is primary, this ADR narrows to a secondary/offline channel favouring the simpler options; resolving the MSIX decision first is the cheapest sequencing, and leaving it open blocks the Phase 6 signed-installer exit criterion.
nodes.norm_label: installer choice sequenced behind the msix decision
